claims.text: The alloy is Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA produced by additive manufacturing with a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
Combining in situ TEM with atomistic simulations can elucidate nanoprecipitate oxidation behavior in this alloy.
In situ TEM and atomistic simulations can reveal elemental redistribution during oxidation.
Elemental redistribution affects the oxidation resistance of the alloy.
The relevant oxidation mechanism consists of elemental redistribution and oxidation reactions at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Under oxidation at 800°C, 1 atm, in O2 for 100 hours, the AM-produced alloy will exhibit a 20% lower oxidation rate than cast and wrought counterparts.
The reduced oxidation rate will correspond to increased oxidation resistance.
The oxidation rate will be below 0.5 nm/h.
The accuracy of atomistic simulations may be limited by the complexity of the HEA and its dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
The representativeness of in situ TEM observations may be limited by the complexity of the HEA and its dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
